title: Transfer an overseas driver licence
summary: Learn how to transfer an overseas driver licence to a NSW licence.
intro:
If you're an Australian citizen or permanent resident, or if you hold a New Zealand driver licence, you can drive in NSW on an overseas licence for 3 months. Within this 3-month period however, you'll need to visit a Service NSW Centre and transfer your overseas licence to a NSW Driver Licence.

You may need to pass a knowledge or driving test, depending on where your overseas licence was issued. View a list of Recognised countries and jurisdictions.

Drivers 75 years or older are required to undergo a medical review and may need to take a practical driving test.

If you're a temporary visa holder or you cannot provide proof of permanent residency, you can apply for a NSW licence as a temporary overseas visitor.

Note: Holders of licences from certain countries may be required to obtain a validation letter from the relevant consulate or licensing authority. For information regarding validation requirements, please call 13 77 88 or visit a service centre.
who_can_apply: Temporary overseas visitor (if unable to provide proof of permanent residency)
what_you_need: Translation (if licence or letter is not in English)
Original translation document (photocopies are not accepted)

how_to_steps.text: Select the 'Download a PDF form' button.
Complete the form and gather your supporting documents.
Visit a service centre and provide the information in person.

more_info.text: Renewal notices are mailed generally within 6 weeks of the card's expiry date. This means you have plenty of time to plan ahead and renew early.
For driver licence renewals or applications, a receipt is provided that allows you to drive until the card arrives in the post. The receipt is valid for 2 months.

faqs.q: How long can I drive in NSW on an overseas licence?
faqs.a: If you are an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or hold a New Zealand licence, you can drive in NSW on an overseas licence for 3 months.

faqs.q: What do I need to do to transfer my licence?
faqs.a: You must visit a Service NSW Centre to transfer your overseas licence to a NSW Driver Licence. You may need to pass a knowledge or driving test.

faqs.q: Are there special requirements for older drivers?
faqs.a: Drivers 75 years or older are required to undergo a medical review and may need to take a practical driving test.
